title: Post-bounce chop – leaders extended, stops getting hit
body:
Market phase = Trend -> Chop transition

Strategy mismatch:
Breakout style used in non-trending conditions

Better approach:

Focus on:
Pullbacks to 10/20 EMA
Tight consolidations

Avoid:
Late-stage breakouts
thesis:
Market is in post-rally digestion phase:

Early trend phase is over -> now rotation + shakeouts
Extended names -> prone to pullbacks
Tight stops getting hit = noise environment

Key shift:
Move from aggressive breakout trading -> defensive, selective approach
lesson_learned: In extended + choppy markets, reduce size, avoid chasing, and let setups come to you.
what_went_well:
Followed system and respected stops
Correctly identified weak market internals
Maintained discipline despite losses
what_went_wrong:
Entered extended stocks
Used tight stops in noisy market
Slight overexposure
Missed partial trailing opportunity (MTARTECH)

title: Using higher timeframe bias to improve swing trade accuracy
one_line_summary: Higher timeframe defines edge, lower timeframe refines execution.
body:
Weekly = direction
Daily = setup
Lower TF = optional refinement.

Best setups:
HTF uptrend + daily pullback
HTF base + daily breakout

Avoid:
Counter-trend trades
Extended entries far from HTF support
observations:
Market recently bounced -> entering digestion
Leaders extended and choppy
Lower timeframe signals unreliable
Higher timeframe trends still intact in select names
thesis:
Higher timeframe (weekly/daily) provides:

Clear trend direction
Reliable structure
Better probability setups

Lower timeframe creates noise -> leading to:

False entries
Frequent stop-outs

Key idea:
Align trades with higher timeframe trend, use daily for execution
lesson_learned: Higher timeframe defines edge, lower timeframe refines execution.
what_went_well:
Better trade selection using HTF bias
Avoided low-quality setups
Reduced unnecessary trades
what_went_wrong:
Occasional early entries on daily
Minor impatience waiting for confirmation
action_plan:
Always start analysis from weekly chart
Trade only in direction of HTF trend
Enter on daily setups (pullback / breakout)
Avoid lower timeframe noise-based decisions
Use 20 EMA for trailing
anchor_thought: Trade what the higher timeframe confirms, not what the lower timeframe tempts.

title: Winning positions: trail structure, not noise
one_line_summary: Adjust trailing style to market phase; hold winners through shakeouts with structure-based exits.
body:
Big transition: easy trend profits -> messy reality of trend continuation.

Current phase behavior (absorption/rotation):
- Breakouts can fail
- Wicks and squats are common
- Price often goes up/down before continuation

Key interpretation:
- Long wicks = liquidity tests/absorption, not automatic reversal
- Doji/squat = pause and decision, not forced exit
- Strong close = institutional control
- Weak close = warning signal, not immediate exit

Core shift:
- In chop/rotation, trailing tight stops causes avoidable stop-outs.
observations: Mismatch identified: trend-phase stop logic was applied in chop-phase market. Stock selection was acceptable; stop style was the main leak.
thesis: Market moves in discomfort, not comfort. Winners often require sitting through shakeouts before the next leg. Trailing must adapt to phase and structure.
lesson_learned: Trail structure, not candles. Use phase-based exits and a 2-day weakness rule to reduce noise exits.
what_went_well:
Correctly identified market-phase transition
Avoided panic exits after single noisy candles
Defined clear framework for holding winners
what_went_wrong:
Previously reacted to single red candles/wicks
Used stops that were too tight for chop
action_plan:
1) Phase-based trailing: early trend -> below base; mid trend -> 20 EMA zone; momentum -> 10 EMA zone.
2) 2-step exit rule: exit only on 2 consecutive weak closes OR strong close below EMA zone.
3) Partial at +10% to +15%: book 30% to 40% for psychological freedom.
4) Use zone trailing (EMA +/- buffer), not exact-line trailing.
5) In chop phase: reduce size and place stops below swing lows/20 EMA zone.
anchor_thought: Do not let a single candle decide the fate of a winning position.
